body:
This comment convinces me that the current behavior serves no purpose:

```
     * Only for Unix we check for more than one file name.
     * For other systems spaces are considered to be part
     * of the file name.
```

It doesn't make sense for this to be platform specific. Filenames may contain spaces on _any platform_. Why should the behavior be different for unix?

Also `:help :argedit` mentions (incorrectly):

> spaces inside the file name are allowed, like with :edit. 

Filed an issue: https://github.com/vim/vim/issues/1414

I agree that the behaviour could be improved and I'm usually for breaking changes, but this?

This will only lead to users complaining about our (as opposed to Vim's) `:edit` being broken. Moreoever, it would also break _many_ plugins, since they all use some variant of:

```viml
execute 'edit' fnameescape(filename_with_spaces)
```

And now, as if filename handling wasn't bad enough already, you have to distinguish between Vim and Neovim all the time.

My in-head cost-benefit calculation says "nope". :>

I didn't foresee any breakage here. Escaped filenames still are handled correctly, no?

The very next block of code under what @tweekmonster linked, removes backslashes.

Hmm, you're right.

I played a bit around with just the block removed that tweekmonster mentioned, and it seems to work as expected already?

```
" edit "foo bar" (there should be only one match)
:e `ls foo*`

" edit "foo bar"
:e foo bar

" edit "foo\bar"
:e foo\\bar

" edit "foo|bar"
:e foo\|bar

" edit "foo\|\ bar"
:exe 'edit' fnameescape('foo\|\ bar')
```

Only one test breaks:

```
[  ERROR   ] /data/repo/neovim/test/functional/legacy/arglist_spec.lua @ 214: argument list commands test for :argedit command
```

(Please use [reactions](https://github.com/blog/2119-add-reactions-to-pull-requests-issues-and-comments) on the first post, if you want to express your feelings without adding new content to this thread, thanks.)
Any chance to port this change on VIM first and only then on Neovim?
sure, ask on vim-dev (or open a ticket von Vims issue tracker). I personally doubt it, that Bram will change it however.
@clobrano We would only make this change if it doesn't break plugins.
Why can't it open multiple buffers instead? Same behavior as when you run `nvim file1 file 2 file3` from the command line.
@fervic `:n` and `:args` already do that, and it also would not be backwards-compatible.
If someone wants to send a PR for this, let's try it out on master and see if the world ends.

issue.title: [RDY] ex_docmd.c: Remove Unix check for multi file args for :edit

repository.name: neovim
repository.description: Vim-fork focused on extensibility and usability

issue.body:
Remove the Unix check for more than one file for :edit. "E172: Only one file
name allowed" was thrown when a non-escaped space was detected in the line.
This unifies the default behaviour of :edit to only accept one file, and try
to treat the rest of the line as a file name when encountering a space.

https://github.com/neovim/neovim/issues/6010
